blocks.html: Fourthly, the shoemaker who shod Martin Guerre deposes that this Martin was shod at twelve points, whereas nevertheless the prisoner is shod only at nine. And another, that the said Martin played well at fencing and at palestrine [wrestling], at which game the prisoner neither does nor understands anything. For the fifth, there are three witnesses, to one of whom, called Jean Espagnol, innkeeper of Touges, the said du Tilh disclosed himself on his return, begging him to say nothing of it: for Martin Guerre was dead, who had given him his property. To the other, called Valentin Rougié, who named him and recognised him as du Tilh, he made a sign with his finger that he should hold his peace. To the third, called Pelegrin de Liberos, he made a like sign and moreover gave two handkerchiefs, with the charge to deliver one to Jean du Tilh his brother.
